title: Finite-ring scalar direct-image comparison using relative cohomological dimension
statement:
Fix a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ and a prime $\ell
e p$. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X	o Y$ a $k$-morphism [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $a:A	o B$ be a unital homomorphism of finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$, with their discrete topologies [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. On the small etale and pro-etale sites use ordinary uncompleted derived categories of constant-ring module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $K\in D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, where pro-etale constructibility is as in [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf], finite Tor amplitude is as in [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and etale constructibility is as in [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. For $Z=X,Y$ and $t=\mathrm{et},\mathrm{proet}$ put $T_Z^t=B_Z\otimes^L_{A_Z}-$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Let $
u_Z:Z_{\mathrm{proet}}	o Z_{\mathrm{et}}$ be the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. There exists $J\in D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ with $
u_X^*J\cong K$; $J_B=T_X^{\mathrm{et}}J$ and $Q=T_Y^{\mathrm{et}}Rf_{*,A}^{\mathrm{et}}J$ are bounded below. Define $\gamma_L^t:T_Y^tRf_{*,A}^tL	o Rf_{*,B}^tT_X^tL$ as the adjunct of
$$f_B^*T_Y^tRf_{*,A}^tL\xrightarrow{\sim}T_X^tf_A^*Rf_{*,A}^tL\xrightarrow{T_X^t(\varepsilon^A_L)}T_X^tL,$$
using the canonical pullback/tensor comparison and module adjunctions [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations, def-kun-projection-formula-map]. Both $\gamma_J^{\mathrm{et}}$ and $\gamma_K^{\mathrm{proet}}$ are isomorphisms in the $B$-module derived categories. After restricting $\gamma_J^{\mathrm{et}}$ to $A$, using the canonical restriction/direct-image comparison [def-kun-scalar-restriction-comparison-maps] and the coefficient pullback identification [def-pur-scalar-pullback-representative-data], it is the specified relative projection map
$$Rf_{*,A}^{\mathrm{et}}J\otimes_A^LB_Y\longrightarrow Rf_{*,A}^{\mathrm{et}}(J\otimes_A^LB_X).$$
Under the canonical tensor comparisons $\delta_Z:T_Z^{\mathrm{proet}}
u_Z^*\cong
u_Z^*T_Z^{\mathrm{et}}$ and direct-image comparisons $ eta^R:
u_Y^*Rf_{*,R}^{\mathrm{et}}\cong Rf_{*,R}^{\mathrm{proet}}
u_X^*$, $R=A,B$, of [lem-sfb-etale-proetale-scalar-mate], the actual maps satisfy
$$Rf_{*,B}^{\mathrm{proet}}(\delta_{X,J})\circ\gamma_{
u_X^*J}^{\mathrm{proet}}= eta^B_{J_B}\circ
u_Y^*(\gamma_J^{\mathrm{et}})\circ\delta_{Y,Rf_{*,A}^{\mathrm{et}}J}\circ T_Y^{\mathrm{proet}}(( eta^A_J)^{-1}).$$
There is no assumption that $a$ is flat, that $B$ has finite projective dimension over $A$, or that $k$ has finite absolute etale cohomological dimension.

proof.text: On each constructible stratum of each cohomology sheaf of K, finite_models_of_fixed_lisse turns slice local constancy and finite geometric stalks into finite constant models. The fixed-module constructible-origin theorem descends each cohomology sheaf to the etale site. Bounded constructible derived descent then supplies an etale complex J, its bounds and an isomorphism nu*J to K. Convert etale constructibility with the existing finite-coefficient predicate comparison.

proof.text: Transport a Tor interval for K through the origin isomorphism. The existing fixed-module torAmplitudeIn_mapDerivedCategory_iff reflects it to J. The existing scalarExtension_lowerBound helper computes restricted scalar extension as tensor with B and uses faithful exact restriction to deduce that J_B has the lower bound of this Tor interval.

source.place: Finite rings paragraph; fixed-module descent, relative finite-constant projection and canonical mate transport

proof.text: A finite ring is Noetherian and additively torsion. B, as an A-module via the given ring map, is finite and finitely presented. Apply the existing module-valued hasFiniteCohomologicalDimensionMorphism implementation of the relative 0F10 theorem to the two structure morphisms and Over.w f. Take the natural part of its integer bound. The proved finiteConstantProjectionComponent_isIso makes the projection at constant B invertible. The canonical constant-sheaf/scalar-restriction isomorphism identifies this coefficient with scalarCoefficient a Y; naturality transfers invertibility to this very projection component.

source.place: Finite rings paragraph; fixed-module descent, relative finite-constant projection and canonical mate transport

proof.text: Apply the existing proved scalarMate_isIso_of_projection helper to the lower bounds for J and J_B and the projection component. This uses the normalized mate equation, the bounded-below direct-image restriction comparison, and exact restriction reflecting isomorphisms; it assumes no absolute cohomological bound on the base field. To obtain the separate lower-bound assertion for Q, compose the scalarTensorIso, this invertible projection component and the canonical coefficient-pullback and tensor identifications. This identifies the restriction of Q with Rf_* of the restriction of J_B. Exact restriction and the left t-exactness of Rf_* give its lower bound, and faithful exact restriction reflects that bound. Apply scalarMate_restrict_eq_projection with these bounded-below witnesses to obtain the required equality of morphisms.

source.place: Finite rings paragraph; fixed-module descent, relative finite-constant projection and canonical mate transport

proof.text: Since f followed by Y to Spec k equals the separated quasi-compact structure morphism of X, cancellation gives that f is separated and quasi-compact, hence quasi-separated. Apply etaleProEtale_scalar_mate to J and J_B. Take eA to be directImageComparisonAmbientIso; its hom is by construction the published ambient comparison. The right side of the transport equality is invertible, since the etale scalar mate, both beta comparisons at the bounded-below inputs, and both delta comparisons are invertible. Cancel the image of delta_X to show the pro-etale scalar mate at nu*J invertible. Naturality of that natural transformation transports invertibility along nu*J isomorphic to K. Return the same transport equality, without changing any normalization.
